title: BTS
summary:
This document is a comprehensive encyclopedia-style article about BTS, the South Korean boy band formed in 2010 and debuted in 2013 under Big Hit Entertainment, consisting of members Jin, Suga, J-Hope, RM, Jimin, V, and Jung Kook. The article begins with an overview of the group's record-breaking achievements, including being the best-selling musical act in South Korean history, becoming the first Korean act to top the Billboard 200, earning Grammy nominations, and their historic chart success with singles like "Dynamite," "Butter," and "Life Goes On."

The document traces the group's complete history chronologically, covering their formation as a hip hop group under CEO Bang Si-hyuk, their early "school trilogy" releases, mainstream breakthrough with "The Most Beautiful Moment in Life" series, international expansion with the "Love Yourself" and "Map of the Soul" album series, their pandemic-era virtual concerts, the anthology album Proof, the members' mandatory South Korean military service (2022–2025), and their highly anticipated reunion and 2026 album Arirang with its accompanying world tour.

Additional sections detail the meaning behind the group's name ("Bulletproof Boy Scouts," later "Beyond the Scene"), their artistry including musical influences ranging from Seo Taiji and Queen to literary works by Hermann Hesse and Nietzsche, their genre-spanning musical style rooted in hip hop, and their socially conscious lyrical themes addressing mental health, youth struggles, and self-love. The article also examines BTS's broader cultural and economic impact on South Korea (estimated at $5 billion annually), their role in cultural diplomacy through UN addresses and presidential envoy appointments, their highly organized global fandom ARMY, commercial endorsements with brands like Samsung and Louis Vuitton, philanthropic efforts including the UNICEF Love Myself campaign, their extensive accolades, member profiles, and listings of their discography, films, and online shows, concluding with cited academic literature and references.
